reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Application, examination, and classification as forest croplands
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1945 p. 672 § 5, A.L. 1974 H.B. 1210, A.L. 1981 H.B. 308, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1348). Covers submitting a forest cropland application to the state forester on commission forms, examination and forwarding of recommendations to the commission, and chapter 254 and regulatory applicability upon approval and classification.

headings.title: Circuit court appeal from refusal to classify
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits an applicant to appeal commission refusal to accept and classify lands to the circuit court where the lands (or major part) are located, with the circuit court's decision final.

headings.title: Minimum acreage and per-acre value limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Bars accepting forest cropland applications for tracts under twenty acres and bars tax-relief classification if land value exceeds $125 per acre or a greater value set by commission regulation.

headings.title: Ineligibility of forest croplands for section 254.225 program
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Bars accepting applications for the section 254.225 cost-share incentive program for lands designated as forest croplands.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–4 and history note (L. 1945 p. 672 § 5 through A.L. 2002 H.B. 1348) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed application, state forester examination, and commission classification in (1), final circuit court appeal from refusal in (2), twenty-acre minimum and $125/acre (or higher regulation-set) value cap in (3), and ineligibility of forest croplands for the section 254.225 program in (4). All 4 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Classification of commission-use lands and county grant rate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1945 p. 672 § 19, A.L. 1955 p. 316, A.L. 1957 p. 311, A.L. 1965 p. 388, A.L. 1974 H.B. 1210, A.L. 1981 H.B. 308). Permits the commission to classify state-conveyed commission-use lands as forest croplands and requires county grants in lieu of taxes from the conservation commission fund at not less than fifty cents per acre per year. Independent review revised title to "commission-use lands" to reflect the body text ("lands conveyed to the state for use of the commission" / "state-owned") alongside the catchline.

headings.title: Deposit of county grants in general revenue fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires counties to place grants in lieu of taxes received under this section into the county's general revenue fund.

headings.title: Annual certification, payment after appropriation, and nonretroactivity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers annual commission certification of acreage and payable amounts to the commissioner of administration and state auditor, treasurer payment authorization after appropriations on or before January 1 following certification, and the express nonretroactivity clause.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–3 and history note (L. 1945 p. 672 § 19 through A.L. 1981 H.B. 308) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked permissive classification of state-owned lands conveyed for commission use and >=$0.50/acre county grants in (1), county general revenue fund deposit in (2), and annual acreage/amount certification, appropriation-conditioned payment by January 1, and nonretroactivity in (3). Revised title (1) to "commission-use lands" to match the statutory text; retained titles (2)–(3).

headings.title: Private management plan approval and partial tax relief
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1945 p. 672 § 20). Permits forest land owners or controllers to develop their own management plans and obtain chapter 254 partial tax relief during compliance, conditioned on commission-form submission and commission approval based on reasonable assurance of accomplishing the law's purposes.

headings.title: Revised working plans, commission finality, and tax-relief procedure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits submitting revised cutting and management working plans after initial approval in commission-prescribed form and periods, makes commission decisions final, and adopts chapter 254 forest cropland procedures to effectuate tax relief.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 1945 p. 672 § 20) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed commission-approved private forest management plans and compliance-conditioned partial tax relief in (1), and revised working plans, finality of commission decisions, and adoption of forest cropland tax-relief procedures in (2). Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Annual private cropland acreage and county grant rate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1945 p. 672 § 10, A.L. 1955 p. 316, A.L. 1957 p. 311, A.L. 1965 p. 388, A.L. 1974 H.B. 1210, A.L. 1981 H.B. 308). Directs the commission to determine accepted privately owned forest cropland acreage in each county as of January 1 annually and pay grants in lieu of taxes from the conservation commission fund at not less than fifty cents per acre per year. Independent review revised "count" to "acreage" to match "number of acres" in the text.

headings.title: Deposit of county grants in general revenue fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires counties to place grants in lieu of taxes received for privately owned forest croplands into each county's general revenue fund.

headings.title: Annual certification, payment after appropriation, and nonretroactivity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers annual commission certification of payable amounts to the commissioner of administration and state auditor, treasurer payment authorization after appropriations on or before the following January 1, and the express nonretroactivity clause.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–3 and history note (L. 1945 p. 672 § 10 through A.L. 1981 H.B. 308) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed annual January 1 private cropland acreage determination and >=$0.50/acre county grant rate in (1), county general revenue fund deposit in (2), and annual payable-amount certification, appropriation-conditioned payment by January 1, and nonretroactivity in (3). Revised "count" to "acreage" in title (1); retained titles (2)–(3).

headings.title: Conditions and duration for continuing classification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1945 p. 672 § 11, A.L. 1974 H.B. 1210). Continues forest cropland classification as long as proper forest conditions and practices are maintained and within chapter 254 time limits.

headings.title: Grounds for cancellation, notice, and return to taxation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Lists grounds for canceling classification (pasture use, failure to restore destroyed tree-growth, removal for other uses, noncomplying changed conditions, or pasture use violating commission regulations), mandates cancellation and notice to county assessor, county clerk, and owner upon noncompliance, and returns the land to ordinary taxation.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 1945 p. 672 § 11, A.L. 1974 H.B. 1210) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed continued classification while proper forest practices are maintained within chapter time limits in (1), and cancellation grounds, mandatory cancellation with notice to assessor, county clerk, and owner, and return to ordinary taxation in (2). Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Authorized cost-share program, reimbursement cap, and forestry standards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 2002 H.B. 1348), and cross-reference note (forest croplands ineligible under 254.040). Grants permissive authority ('may administer') for a private-land sustainable forestry cost-share incentive program reimbursing up to fifty percent of eligible precommercial forestry activity costs conducted under best management practices and sustainable forestry principles.

headings.title: Program applications, procedures, and commission acceptance criteria
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history note, and cross-reference note to section 254.040. Permits forest landowners to apply to the state forester on commission forms and directs the commission to specify application procedures and acceptance criteria.

headings.title: Minimum acreage and annual per-person incentive cap
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, history note, and cross-reference note to section 254.040. Bars accepting applications for tracts under forty acres and caps total incentives to any person at five thousand dollars in any calendar year. Independent review revised title to clarify that the $5,000 calendar-year limit is per person.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–3, history note (L. 2002 H.B. 1348), and cross-reference note (forest croplands ineligible under 254.040), and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Verified permissive private-land cost-share program, 50% precommercial cap, and BMP/sustainable forestry standards in (1), landowner applications and commission criteria in (2), and 40-acre minimum plus $5,000 per-person calendar-year cap in (3). Retained titles (1)–(2); revised title (3) to clarify the per-person annual cap.

headings.title: Enforcement duties of commission agents, officers, and prosecutors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1945 p. 672 § 28). Requires authorized commission agents to assist in enforcing chapter 254 and commission rules, and requires sheriffs, marshals, constables, deputies, police officers, and prosecuting attorneys and assistants within their counties to aid diligently in enforcement. Independent review revised title to explicitly include prosecuting attorneys and their assistants alongside commission agents and peace/police officers.

headings.title: Warrantless arrest authority and prompt court proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits such officers and agents to arrest without warrant persons caught in view violating or with good reason to believe are violating or have violated chapter 254 or commission rules, and requires bringing them forthwith before an associate circuit judge or court with jurisdiction for prompt criminal adjudication.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 1945 p. 672 § 28) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed enforcement duties of authorized commission agents, sheriffs, marshals, constables, deputies, police officers, and prosecuting attorneys and assistants in (1), and warrantless arrest authority and prompt criminal proceedings in (2). Revised title (1) to include prosecutors explicitly; retained title (2).

headings.title: Fire control and timber trespass assistance for woodlands
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1945 p. 672 § 21). Covers intensifying fire control and timber trespass activities and permissively extending them to all state woodlands deemed in need by the commission within available funds, regardless of whether lands are classified as forest croplands.

headings.title: Owner-funded applications for added forest fire protection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits any owner to apply to the commission for special forest fire control exceeding general chapter funds by subscribing at least three cents per acre per year for added protection deemed advisable and desirable by the commission.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 1945 p. 672 § 21) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed intensified fire control and timber trespass assistance extendable to all woodlands within available funds regardless of forest-cropland classification in (1), and owner applications for added forest fire protection by subscribing at least three cents per acre per year in (2). Both drafted titles retained.
